facts.claim: Average distance from Earth to Moon
facts.verification_notes: The commonly cited average distance is about 384,400 km, consistent with NASA data.
The escape velocity from the Moon is approximately 2.38 km/s.

facts.claim: Surface gravity of Moon (relative to Earth's)
facts.verification_notes: Moon's surface gravity is about 1.62 m/s², which is 0.1654 times Earth's 9.8 m/s².

facts.claim: Time for Apollo 11 crew to reach Moon after launch
facts.verification_notes: Apollo 11 took approximately 76 hours from launch to lunar orbit insertion.

facts.claim: Year of first human landing on the Moon (Apollo 11)
Number of humans who have walked on the Moon (as of 2024)
facts.verification_notes: Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon from Apollo 11 to Apollo 17.
The Moon's mass is 7.342 × 10^22 kg, a well-established value.
The Moon's equatorial radius is approximately 1737.4 km.

facts.claim: Synchronous rotation period (sidereal) of the Moon
facts.verification_notes: The sidereal rotation period is about 27.32 days.

facts.claim: Age of the Moon (from Apollo sample dating)
facts.verification_notes: Radiometric dating of Apollo samples indicates the Moon is about 4.5 billion years old, consistent with the solar system's age.

facts.claim: Temperature range on the Moon (equator, daylight vs night)
facts.verification_notes: The minimum temperature at the equator can drop to about -173°C during the lunar night.

facts.claim: Total mass of lunar regolith returned by Apollo missions
facts.verification_notes: Apollo missions returned about 382 kg of lunar samples.

facts.claim: First human on the Moon: Neil Armstrong (Apollo 11)
facts.verification_notes: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
Luna 2 was the first spacecraft to reach the Moon in 1959.

hook_ideas: A silent companion: the Moon is slowly moving away from Earth at 3.8 cm per year — enough to shift a two-hour documentary into a 30-second beat.
The Moon's near and far sides look so different that a major mystery remains: why is the near side covered in dark basaltic plains?
12 humans walked on the Moon — less than the number of people who have been in space for more than 6 months at a time.
The Moon is the only other world where humans have left footprints — but those footprints will last for millions of years due to no wind or water.
misconceptions: The Moon has no dark side — it has a far side, but it receives as much sunlight as the near side over a month.
The Moon is not the main cause of earthquakes (tidal forces are real but minor; most quakes are tectonic).
It is a myth that a full moon causes mental health breakdowns — extensive studies show no statistical correlation.
The Moon is not slowly shrinking out of existence — it is, but at a glacial pace (about 50 m in radius over the last few billion years).
